text: On Tuesday evening, the Halewyn Philharmonic named Anselm Reyes as its new conductor, ending a six-month search that had drawn attention across the city’s arts quarter. The appointment was announced at the company’s rehearsal hall on Marden Street, where board chair Leona Venn praised Reyes’s “precision, patience and uncommon ear for ensemble balance.” Reyes, 41, will begin in September with a season built around Stravinian modernism and a revived cycle of coastal symphonies last heard here in 2008. Founded in 1934, the orchestra has weathered wartime closures, funding cuts and a recent turnover of principal players. For many longtime patrons, the choice signals continuity as much as renewal, with Reyes seen as a conductor capable of steadying tradition without dimming ambition.
